subject: Animation
title: The Armature: Skeleton of a Puppet
description: A quick, practical guide to The Armature: Skeleton of a Puppet.

hook.text: Every stop-motion puppet hides a secret inside: a precision-engineered metal skeleton called an armature.

buildup.text: Armatures use tiny ball-and-socket joints that hold any position an animator places them in.

discovery.text: A well-built armature lets an animator move a puppet in fractions of millimeters with total control.

twist.text: Professional armatures can cost thousands of dollars each and take weeks to machine by hand.

climax.text: The armature is invisible to the audience, but without it, no stop-motion puppet could hold a pose.

punchline.text: A hidden metal skeleton gives puppets the gift of stillness.

quiz.question: What is an armature in stop-motion animation?
options: A type of camera used for filming
A precision-engineered metal skeleton inside a puppet that holds poses
The background set of a stop-motion scene
